localFacts.fact: Iberia allows a cabin bag of up to 10 kg and max. 56 x 40 x 25 cm; by folded length the TC40 (50 cm) fits, the RT90C (59 cm) and the Tri-Pier (65 cm) do not.
Since 2014 the sky of the Parque Nacional del Teide is a 'Destino Starlight' (Fundación Starlight); the cable-car base station at about 2.356 m is used for guided stargazing.

A Spanish owner on Astrónomo.org fitted the AM5's PE200 to his old Sky-Watcher NEQ6 steel tripod with a 3/8" threaded rod of a little over 30 cm, the silver AM5 adapter inside the extension, and found it clearly steadier than the carbon tripod.
Spanish terms: trípode, extensor de columna / columna (PE200), trípode-columna (Tri-Pier), montura armónica, contrapeso, puesta en estación, carga útil, bandeja portaoculares, rosca de 3/8".

localPainPoints.pain: The carbon tripod lacks mass for heavier scopes.
localPainPoints.fix: Load the weight bag; for a C8 or heavier move to steel legs (LiteRoc) or the Tri-Pier, or reuse an old steel tripod with the PE200 and a 3/8" rod.

quotes.text: su falta de masa determina que pueda ser crítico cuando montamos un equipo con cierto peso

localPainPoints.pain: Tip-over: without counterweight the centre of gravity can leave the leg circle.
localPainPoints.fix: Hang weight low, keep the legs spread wide, add the counterweight above 10 kg payload as the forum post says the AM5 manual advises; heavy loads go on the Tri-Pier.

quotes.text: Una vez el centro de gravedad se sale del círculo que forma las patas del trípode, se va a caer.

localGain.point: Iberia cabin size vs folded length: only the TC40 fits.
Spanish DIY route: old NEQ6 steel tripod + PE200 + 3/8" threaded rod.
Teide as a Starlight destination for travel imaging with the TC40.
